producer_report.summary:
I created docs/design/requirements-map.md and added a row for it to the README map and an entry to the CHANGELOG. No code, governance file or BRIEF.md changed.

The doc has:
- **Requirements table:** one row per BRIEF.md requirement, addenda included. That covers O1–O5, the environment facts, the standards, the boundaries, A1–A13, S1–S7, D1–D3, the required order, scope, stopping, the acceptance tests, and the eleven addenda. Each row has a status, an owning design doc, serving work and file:line evidence.
- **Corrections from the earlier attempt:**
  - The O1 `built` row cites the status line of docs/design/athena-v0.md (line 3) and the work-item line (line 8). It does not cite D46.
  - The permission to use GitHub features (BRIEF.md:129) and the ban on pushing upstream (BRIEF.md:130) are on separate, correctly numbered rows.
- **Strategy view (A1):** goals, bets, risks, open questions and next steps, plus how it is kept current. The kept-current method is: any job that changes a row's status edits the page, `athena status` stays the source for job state, the as-of date changes on every edit, and no test enforces any of this yet.
- **Roadmap:** items Q1–Q10 with dependencies, an ordered sequence with the reasons for it, and what would change the order.
- **Alternatives considered:** a table of the options I rejected and why.

**Limits:**
- records/ was not in my snapshot, so serving work is named by decision entry and roadmap label, not job id.
- I could not read the live queue, so the roadmap comes from the build plans and pull-in tables in the existing design docs.

**Checks:** `cargo fmt --all --check` passes. `cargo test --locked -p xtask` passes (4 and 9 tests, including the boundary scan). A search of the three touched files for the banned words found nothing. I did not run clippy or the full workspace tests.

checks_run.note: Includes the boundary scan and docs policy tests; 4 + 9 tests passed. The full workspace test and clippy were not run (docs-only change).

checks_run.command: Grep for the banned words and fragments over the three touched files

open_issues: Serving jobs are named by decision entry and roadmap label, not by job id, because records/ is absent from the snapshot. The live queue was not read, so the roadmap items come from the docs' own build plans and pull-in tables.
Statuses that depend on the records (whether later work went through Athena, the intervention trend, calibration) are marked as such and not asserted.
The strategy view is kept current by convention only. No test checks the page's citations. The page names that as a later item (Q6).
Citation line numbers were checked by hand against what I read. They have no automated guard.
Not run: cargo clippy and the full workspace tests. The change touches no Rust.
mistakes: First draft quoted 'reviewed before they are built' as if verbatim from BRIEF.md. It is not. I reworded it to a paraphrase and cited BRIEF.md:121.
First draft cited BRIEF.md:79-81 for the effort-split rule. The text is on line 81. Fixed.
First draft said both unbuilt designs had a pending review. Only parallel-jobs says so. Fixed.
learnings: BRIEF.md line map: GitHub-features permission is line 129 and the upstream-push ban is line 130. Effort-split text is line 81 (O4 spans 78-82). Addenda start at line 445.

docs/design/athena-v0.md line 3 holds the status line ('accepted. Revision 2 answered independent review 1'), and line 8 names the bootstrap work item. Lines 1572-1599 are the table of left-out items with their pull-in triggers.
D46 (docs/decisions.md:1004) is about per-job build directories, not the O1 build status.
The native-pr-landing design says only 'proposed (D72)' on line 3. Only parallel-jobs says its review is pending, and no review file exists for either.
The Bash hook rejects tail and pipes. Only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm are allowed.
The policy tests in xtask scan docs/*.md for the banned boundary terms, so a doc can fail the test check.
desires: Read access to records/ so statuses and serving job ids could come from real job records instead of decision entries.
A script that checks every quoted string against its cited file and line.
